# CLI reference

`nebulactrl` is a command line client for the control plane REST API. It authenticates with an API token; see [API tokens and scopes](../operations/teams.md) and [the API reference](api.md).

## Global options

Manage NebulaCtrl projects, services, deployments and servers through the control plane REST API.

A <service> is a service ID or project/env/slug. Configuration lives in ~/.config/nebulactrl/config.json (override with NEBULACTRL_CONFIG; NEBULACTRL_URL and NEBULACTRL_TOKEN override its fields).

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--idempotency-key` | string |  | Idempotency-Key for mutating calls (default: random per invocation) |
| `--insecure` | bool |  | allow the API token to travel over plain http to a host other than this machine (default: https only) |
| `--json` | bool |  | print machine-readable JSON |

Exit codes: `0` success, `1` failure, `2` wrong flags or arguments.

## nebulactrl backups

Back up and restore managed databases.

```
nebulactrl backups
```

### nebulactrl backups create

Back up a database now.

```
nebulactrl backups create <database> --destination <name|id> [flags]
```

Options:

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--destination` | string |  | destination name or id |
| `--timeout` | duration | `2h0m0s` | give up waiting after this long (with --wait) |
| `--wait` | bool |  | wait for the backup to finish; exit non-zero unless it succeeded |

### nebulactrl backups destinations

Manage backup destinations (S3-compatible buckets, server directories).

```
nebulactrl backups destinations
```

#### nebulactrl backups destinations add

Add a backup destination.

```
nebulactrl backups destinations add --name <n> --kind s3|local [flags]
```

The S3 secret key is never taken as an argument (it would show in process lists): pass --secret-key-file
(`-` reads standard input) or set NEBULACTRL_BACKUP_SECRET_KEY.

Options:

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--access-key` | string |  | S3 access key id |
| `--bucket` | string |  | S3 bucket |
| `--endpoint` | string |  | S3 endpoint URL (empty: AWS) |
| `--kind` | string |  | s3 or local |
| `--local-dir` | string |  | local destinations: sub-directory of the agent's backup directory |
| `--name` | string |  | destination name |
| `--path-style` | bool |  | path-style addressing (MinIO, SeaweedFS, Garage) |
| `--prefix` | string |  | key prefix |
| `--region` | string |  | S3 region |
| `--secret-key-file` | string |  | file holding the S3 secret key (`-` for stdin) |

#### nebulactrl backups destinations ls

List backup destinations.

```
nebulactrl backups destinations ls
```

OFF-SITE is "yes" for an external S3 bucket and "no" for a directory on a server and for the built-in backup storage, which
lives on the control-plane host: backups kept there are lost with that host, so add an external destination as well.

#### nebulactrl backups destinations rm

Remove a backup destination.

```
nebulactrl backups destinations rm <name|id>
```

#### nebulactrl backups destinations test

Write, read and delete a probe object through a server's agent.

```
nebulactrl backups destinations test <name|id> --server <server-id> [flags]
```

Options:

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--server` | string |  | server whose agent runs the test |

### nebulactrl backups lock

Keep a backup forever (never pruned or deleted).

```
nebulactrl backups lock <backup-id>
```

### nebulactrl backups ls

List a database's backups.

```
nebulactrl backups ls <database>
```

### nebulactrl backups restore

Restore a backup into a new database (default) or in place.

```
nebulactrl backups restore <backup-id> [flags]
```

By default the backup is restored into a NEW sibling database with fresh credentials; the original is
untouched. With --in-place the database is overwritten after a safety backup; --confirm must equal its slug.

Options:

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--confirm` | string |  | the database's slug (required with --in-place) |
| `--in-place` | bool |  | overwrite the database instead of restoring into a new one |
| `--name` | string |  | name of the new database |
| `--server` | string |  | server id for the new database |
| `--timeout` | duration | `2h0m0s` | give up waiting after this long (with --wait) |
| `--wait` | bool |  | wait for the restore to finish; exit non-zero unless it succeeded |

### nebulactrl backups rm

Delete a backup and its stored object.

```
nebulactrl backups rm <backup-id>
```

### nebulactrl backups schedules

Manage recurring backups.

```
nebulactrl backups schedules
```

#### nebulactrl backups schedules add

Schedule recurring backups.

```
nebulactrl backups schedules add <database> --destination <name|id> --cron "0 3 * * *" [flags]
```

Options:

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--cron` | string |  | 5-field cron expression or @daily/@hourly/… |
| `--destination` | string |  | destination name or id |
| `--keep` | int | `7` | keep the newest N backups (0 = no limit) |
| `--keep-days` | int |  | delete backups older than N days (0 = never) |
| `--timezone` | string | `UTC` | IANA timezone |

#### nebulactrl backups schedules ls

List a database's backup schedules.

```
nebulactrl backups schedules ls <database>
```

#### nebulactrl backups schedules rm

Remove a backup schedule.

```
nebulactrl backups schedules rm <schedule-id>
```

### nebulactrl backups unlock

Allow retention to prune a backup again.

```
nebulactrl backups unlock <backup-id>
```

## nebulactrl build-settings

Show or set the team's default build location and registry.

```
nebulactrl build-settings [--build-location target|build-server] [--registry <id|none>] [flags]
```

Without flags, prints the team default. With flags (administrators only), replaces it. Projects and services can
override it. When no usable build server or registry exists a build falls back to the target server.

Options:

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--build-location` | string |  | target or build-server |
| `--registry` | string |  | default registry ID (none clears) |

## nebulactrl config

Manage a project from a nebula.toml file.

```
nebulactrl config
```

A nebula.toml file describes one project: its services, domains, variables (names and references, never secret values), tasks, monitors, backup schedules, scaling, volumes and per-environment overrides.

The lifecycle is validate, plan, apply. `apply` stages changes exactly like a dashboard edit, applies the settings that take effect at once, and deploys only with --deploy.
Start from `config export` of a live project, or `config init` for a new repository.

Exit codes: validate 0 valid, 1 invalid. plan 0 ok (with --detailed-exit-code: 0 no changes, 3 changes pending), 1 invalid or failed. apply 0 applied or nothing to do, 1 blocked, failed or partial. 2 wrong flags.

### nebulactrl config apply

Apply a nebula.toml to an environment.

```
nebulactrl config apply [flags]
```

Plans again inside one transaction and applies: changes that need a deploy are staged like a dashboard edit, settings that take effect at once run afterwards. Nothing is deployed unless you pass --deploy.
Pass --plan-id (or --plan <file> from `config plan --plan-out`) to fail with plan_stale when anything changed since that plan; use the same --only and --prune as when planning. Without it the apply plans and applies atomically.
--prune also deletes sub-resources the file owned before and no longer lists (variables, domains, volume attachments, networks, links, tasks, backup schedules); services, databases and stored data are never deleted. It needs --yes.
Exit 0 when applied or nothing to do; 1 when blocked, failed or partial (the result lists the failed steps; apply again to converge).

Examples:

```sh
nebulactrl config apply --env staging
nebulactrl config apply --env production --plan plan.json --deploy --wait
```

Options:

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--deploy` | bool |  | deploy the services this apply touched that now have staged changes |
| `--env` | stringArray |  | environment ID, slug or name; repeat to plan several (optional when the project has one standard environment) |
| `-f, --file` | string |  | path of the file (default: nebula.toml in the current directory, else in a parent directory up to the git root) |
| `--from-git` | bool |  | read the file through the environment's repository binding instead of the local file (needs --project) |
| `--only` | stringArray |  | restrict the apply to this file key path (repeatable); use the same value as when planning |
| `--plan` | string |  | take the plan id and the environment from a file written by `config plan --plan-out` |
| `--plan-id` | string |  | fail with plan_stale unless the plan is still this one (pl_…) |
| `--project` | string |  | project ID, slug or name (default: the `project` key of the file) |
| `--prune` | bool |  | also delete sub-resources the file owned before and no longer lists (needs --yes) |
| `--timeout` | duration | `30m0s` | give up waiting after this long (with --wait) |
| `--verbose` | bool |  | list every field of new services and the live members the file does not mention |
| `--wait` | bool |  | with --deploy: wait for the deployments; exit non-zero unless they all succeeded |
| `--yes` | bool |  | confirm --prune |

### nebulactrl config export

Write the live state of a project as a nebula.toml.

```
nebulactrl config export [flags]
```

Reads the live project and prints a nebula.toml that plans to no changes against it. Only keys that differ from their defaults or that a file already owns are written; secrets are written as names only. The output is deterministic, so diffs stay small.
With --all every standard environment is exported and factored into base definitions plus [environments.<slug>] overrides. Things the format cannot express are listed in a trailing comment and as warnings on stderr.

Examples:

```sh
nebulactrl config export --project acme-shop --env production -o nebula.toml
nebulactrl config export --project acme-shop --all
```

Options:

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--all` | bool |  | export every standard environment, factored into base definitions and [environments.<slug>] overrides |
| `--base` | string |  | with --all: the environment slug the base definitions come from (default: the production environment, else the first) |
| `--defaults` | bool |  | also write keys that equal their default |
| `--env` | string |  | environment ID, slug or name to export |
| `-o, --out` | string |  | write to this file instead of stdout |
| `--project` | string |  | project ID, slug or name (default: the `project` key of the file) |

### nebulactrl config init

Write a starter nebula.toml for this repository.

```
nebulactrl config init [flags]
```

Looks at the directory (Dockerfile, compose file, package.json, go.mod, pyproject.toml, Gemfile, composer.json, .env.example, the git remote) and writes a commented nebula.toml with one service. It works offline and never overwrites a file without --force.
With --project and --env it does not guess: it exports the live environment instead, like `config export`. Review the file, then run `config validate`, `config plan` and `config apply`.

Examples:

```sh
nebulactrl config init
nebulactrl config init --image ghcr.io/acme/api:1.4 --name api
nebulactrl config init --project acme-shop --env production
```

Options:

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--env` | string |  | with --project: the environment to export |
| `-f, --file` | string |  | where to write the file (default: nebula.toml in the current directory) |
| `--force` | bool |  | overwrite an existing file |
| `--git` | string |  | repository URL of the git service (default: the origin remote of this repository) |
| `--image` | string |  | scaffold an image service for this image instead of looking at the repository |
| `--name` | string |  | display name of the service (its slug is derived from it, default: the directory name) |
| `--project` | string |  | project slug to write into the file; with --env, export that project's live environment instead |

### nebulactrl config plan

Show what applying a nebula.toml would change.

```
nebulactrl config plan [flags]
```

Reads nothing but the file and the live project and changes nothing. Every change is labelled staged (takes effect on the next deploy) or applies at once. Secret values never appear: they are masked.
With --detailed-exit-code the exit code is 0 for no changes, 3 for pending changes and 1 for an invalid plan. Several --env flags print one plan per environment; --plan-out then inserts the environment slug before the file extension.

Examples:

```sh
nebulactrl config plan --env production
nebulactrl config plan --env staging --plan-out plan.json
nebulactrl config plan --env production --detailed-exit-code --json
```

Options:

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--detailed-exit-code` | bool |  | exit 0 when there are no changes, 3 when changes are pending, 1 when the plan is invalid |
| `--env` | stringArray |  | environment ID, slug or name; repeat to plan several (optional when the project has one standard environment) |
| `-f, --file` | string |  | path of the file (default: nebula.toml in the current directory, else in a parent directory up to the git root) |
| `--from-git` | bool |  | read the file through the environment's repository binding instead of the local file (needs --project) |
| `--only` | stringArray |  | restrict the plan to this file key path, e.g. services.web or services.web.variables.NODE_ENV (repeatable) |
| `--plan-out` | string |  | write the plan (JSON) to this file; pass it to `config apply --plan` |
| `--project` | string |  | project ID, slug or name (default: the `project` key of the file) |
| `--prune` | bool |  | also plan deleting sub-resources the file owned before and no longer lists |
| `--verbose` | bool |  | list every field of new services and the live members the file does not mention |

### nebulactrl config schema

Print the JSON Schema of nebula.toml.

```
nebulactrl config schema [flags]
```

Prints the JSON Schema this CLI was built with. With --remote it fetches /schema/nebula.toml.json from the control plane you are logged in to, which may be newer. Point an editor at it with a `#:schema <url>` first line.

Options:

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--remote` | bool |  | fetch the schema from the control plane instead of printing the embedded one |

### nebulactrl config source

Show or change where an environment reads its nebula.toml.

```
nebulactrl config source
```

An environment can be bound to a repository file (connection, repository, branch, path). On every push the control plane reads the file at the pushed commit and flags services whose settings differ from it; with auto-apply on, a non-production environment stages the file by itself. Production never auto-applies. Auto-apply is a control-plane setting, not a key of the file.

#### nebulactrl config source check

Read the bound file now and compare it with the environment.

```
nebulactrl config source check [flags]
```

Reads the file at the branch head (or at --sha) and updates the sync state. Exit 1 when the file is invalid, not found, unreachable or could not be read; a file that differs is reported, not an error.

Options:

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--env` | string |  | environment ID, slug or name (optional when the project has one standard environment) |
| `--project` | string |  | project ID, slug or name (default: the `project` key of the nebula.toml found from here) |
| `--sha` | string |  | read the file at this commit instead of the branch head |

#### nebulactrl config source clear

Remove the binding of an environment.

```
nebulactrl config source clear [flags]
```

Clears the explicit binding and switches auto-apply off. What the file already owns stays owned.

Options:

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--env` | string |  | environment ID, slug or name (optional when the project has one standard environment) |
| `--project` | string |  | project ID, slug or name (default: the `project` key of the nebula.toml found from here) |

#### nebulactrl config source set

Bind an environment to a nebula.toml in a repository.

```
nebulactrl config source set [flags]
```

Only the flags you pass change; the rest of the binding stays. --auto-apply needs the admin scope and is refused for production environments.

Examples:

```sh
nebulactrl config source set --env staging --repo acme/shop --branch develop
nebulactrl config source set --env staging --connection github-acme --path deploy/nebula.toml --auto-apply
```

Options:

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--auto-apply` | bool |  | stage the file on every push (not for production; needs the admin scope) |
| `--branch` | string |  | branch the file is read from |
| `--connection` | string |  | git connection ID or name that can read the repository |
| `--env` | string |  | environment ID, slug or name (optional when the project has one standard environment) |
| `--no-auto-apply` | bool |  | switch auto-apply off |
| `--path` | string |  | path of the file in the repository (default: nebula.toml) |
| `--project` | string |  | project ID, slug or name (default: the `project` key of the nebula.toml found from here) |
| `--repo` | string |  | repository as owner/name |

#### nebulactrl config source show

Show the file binding and sync state of an environment.

```
nebulactrl config source show [flags]
```

Options:

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--env` | string |  | environment ID, slug or name (optional when the project has one standard environment) |
| `--project` | string |  | project ID, slug or name (default: the `project` key of the nebula.toml found from here) |

### nebulactrl config validate

Check a nebula.toml.

```
nebulactrl config validate [flags]
```

Sends the file to the control plane, which checks it against the project's real servers, connections and services, and prints every diagnostic as file:line:column: severity[code] path: message. Exit 1 when there is any error.
With --offline nothing is sent: the file is parsed, merged and checked statically on this machine (strict keys, types, references, limits), without names or live state.

Examples:

```sh
nebulactrl config validate
nebulactrl config validate --env staging
nebulactrl config validate --offline --json
```

Options:

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--env` | string |  | also check the file as resolved for this environment (slug; with --offline the key of an [environments.<slug>] block) |
| `-f, --file` | string |  | path of the file (default: nebula.toml in the current directory, else in a parent directory up to the git root) |
| `--offline` | bool |  | check on this machine only: parse, strict keys, merge and static validation; no names or live state |
| `--project` | string |  | project ID, slug or name (default: the `project` key of the file) |

## nebulactrl databases

Manage managed databases.

```
nebulactrl databases
```

### nebulactrl databases create

Create a managed database (staged until deployed).

```
nebulactrl databases create --project <project> --env <env> --engine <engine> [--version <v>] [--name <name>] [--flavor postgis] [--database <db>] [--server <server>] [--accept-license] [flags]
```

Options:

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--accept-license` | bool |  | acknowledge the licence of a source-available engine (MongoDB, Redis) |
| `--database` | string |  | database name (default: app) |
| `--engine` | string |  | postgres, mysql, mariadb, valkey, redis, mongodb or clickhouse |
| `--env` | string |  | environment ID, slug or name |
| `--flavor` | string |  | image variant, e.g. postgis |
| `--name` | string |  | display name (default: the engine name) |
| `--project` | string |  | project ID, slug or name |
| `--server` | string |  | target server ID or name |
| `--version` | string |  | major version (default: the engine's default) |

### nebulactrl databases engines

List the database engines and versions.

```
nebulactrl databases engines
```

### nebulactrl databases info

Show a database's engine, exports and last reported state.

```
nebulactrl databases info <service>
```

### nebulactrl databases promote

Promote a read replica to primary (manual).

```
nebulactrl databases promote <replica> [--yes] [--accept-data-loss] [flags]
```

Prints the promotion plan. With --yes it promotes: a switchover while the old primary is reachable (it is frozen, stopped and fenced; no data is lost) or a forced promote otherwise (needs --accept-data-loss: what the replica had not received is lost). The old primary is fenced and never runs as a primary again. Variables that reference it are rewritten as staged changes. Manual: NebulaCtrl does not detect failures or switch automatically.

Options:

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--accept-data-loss` | bool |  | accept losing what the replica had not received (forced promote) |
| `--yes` | bool |  | promote |

### nebulactrl databases rebuild

Rebuild a replica, or a fenced old primary as a replica of the new primary.

```
nebulactrl databases rebuild <replica-or-fenced-primary> [--follow <new-primary>] [flags]
```

Clones the primary again into a new data volume; the old volume is kept until it is deleted.

Options:

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--follow` | string |  | the new primary a fenced old primary should follow (default: the replica that was promoted) |

### nebulactrl databases replicas

Manage PostgreSQL read replicas.

```
nebulactrl databases replicas
```

#### nebulactrl databases replicas add

Add a read replica of a PostgreSQL primary.

```
nebulactrl databases replicas add <primary> --server <server> [--name <name>] [--dry-run] [--accept-mesh-changes] [flags]
```

Creates a read replica service in the primary's environment and clones the primary into it. The replica runs on the primary's server or, with the server mesh enabled on both, on another server. Replication is asynchronous and manual: nothing is detected or switched automatically. --dry-run prints the plan only.

Options:

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--accept-mesh-changes` | bool |  | confirm that the replica adds tailnet devices |
| `--dry-run` | bool |  | only print the plan |
| `--name` | string |  | display name (default: <primary>-replica-<n>) |
| `--server` | string |  | server ID or name the replica runs on |

#### nebulactrl databases replicas ls

List the read replicas of a database and their lag.

```
nebulactrl databases replicas ls <primary-or-replica>
```

#### nebulactrl databases replicas rm

Remove a read replica.

```
nebulactrl databases replicas rm <replica> --yes [flags]
```

Deletes the replica's container and data volume, drops its slot, role and pg_hba.conf line on the primary and releases its mesh link.

Options:

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--yes` | bool |  | confirm the removal |

### nebulactrl databases restore

Restore a database from a dump file on this machine.

```
nebulactrl databases restore <database> --file <dump> [--name <name>] [--server <server>] [--in-place --confirm <slug> [--destination <dest>]] [flags]
```

Uploads a dump file and restores it into a managed database: a pg_dump file (custom -Fc, tar -Ft or plain SQL, optionally
.gz), a mysqldump / mariadb-dump SQL file (optionally .gz) or a mongodump --archive file. The format is detected from the file.
The file is streamed through the control plane to the server's agent; nothing is stored on the way, and the default limit is 5 GiB.

By default the dump is restored into a NEW sibling database with fresh credentials (the original is untouched): point your
apps at it when you are satisfied. With --in-place the database's data is replaced after a safety backup; --confirm must
equal its slug, and --destination names the backup destination of the safety backup (default: the one of its schedule).

Examples:

```sh
nebulactrl databases restore shop/production/postgres --file shop.pgdump
  nebulactrl databases restore shop/production/postgres --file shop.sql.gz --in-place --confirm postgres --destination s3
```

Options:

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--confirm` | string |  | the database's slug (required with --in-place) |
| `--destination` | string |  | backup destination (id or name) of the safety backup (--in-place) |
| `--file` | string |  | the dump file to restore (required) |
| `--in-place` | bool |  | replace the database's data instead of restoring into a new database |
| `--name` | string |  | name of the new database |
| `--server` | string |  | server id for the new database |
| `--timeout` | duration | `2h0m0s` | give up waiting for the new database, and again for the restore, after this long |
| `--wait` | bool | `true` | wait for the restore to finish; exit non-zero unless it succeeded (--wait=false returns once the file is uploaded) |

### nebulactrl databases reveal

Print a connection string (audited as secret.reveal).

```
nebulactrl databases reveal <service> [--key DATABASE_URL] [flags]
```

Prints one derived connection variable in plain text to stdout. The action is recorded in the audit log and needs the deployments:write scope.

Options:

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--key` | string |  | export to reveal (default: the connection URL) |

### nebulactrl databases rotate

Rotate the database password and stage its consumers.

```
nebulactrl databases rotate <service> [--dry-run] [flags]
```

Options:

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--dry-run` | bool |  | only print the plan |

### nebulactrl databases upgrade

Plan (default) or run a database version upgrade.

```
nebulactrl databases upgrade <service> <version> [--yes] [flags]
```

Prints the upgrade plan. With --yes it runs the upgrade: in-place engines stage the new image; PostgreSQL majors are converted with pg_upgrade into a new volume and then staged. Take a backup first.

Options:

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--yes` | bool |  | apply the upgrade |

## nebulactrl deployments

Inspect and roll back deployments.

```
nebulactrl deployments
```

### nebulactrl deployments cancel

Cancel a running deployment.

```
nebulactrl deployments cancel <deployment-id>
```

Cancels a deployment at whatever step it has reached. Before the agent started it the deployment ends as canceled at once.
Once the agent runs it, the agent is asked to abort: a build is killed, the new containers are removed, routes are restored and a stopped previous release is started again, so the current release keeps serving.
The deployment ends as canceled when the agent reports back (check with `deployments status`). Once the new release is live it is too late and the deployment finishes.

### nebulactrl deployments download-logs

Download a deployment's build and deploy log as a file.

```
nebulactrl deployments download-logs <deployment-id> [flags]
```

Writes the deployment's persisted lines (build, deploy and runtime streams; at most 10,000) in the order
they were recorded, as plain text (`<time> [<stream>] <line>`) or NDJSON. Secret values are masked on the
server. --streams all adds the agent's verbose debug trace.

Examples:

```sh
nebulactrl deployments download-logs 6f1c0d5e-… -o build.log
```

Options:

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--format` | string | `txt` | file format: txt or ndjson |
| `--from` | string |  | only lines at or after this time: RFC 3339, a date, or a duration ago (24h) |
| `-o, --output` | string |  | write to this file instead of stdout (created with mode 0600) |
| `--streams` | string |  | all, or a comma-separated list of build, deploy, runtime, debug (default: build, deploy, runtime) |
| `--to` | string |  | only lines before this time (same forms as --from) |

### nebulactrl deployments ls

List the deployments of a service.

```
nebulactrl deployments ls <service>
```

### nebulactrl deployments rollback

Redeploy the release of a previous deployment.

```
nebulactrl deployments rollback <deployment-id> [flags]
```

Creates a new deployment that points at the release of the given deployment.
Application image and configuration only. Databases, volumes and external services are not rolled back.

Options:

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--timeout` | duration | `30m0s` | give up waiting after this long (with --wait) |
| `--wait` | bool |  | wait for the rollback to finish; exit non-zero unless it succeeded |

### nebulactrl deployments status

Show a deployment and its step timeline.

```
nebulactrl deployments status <deployment-id>
```

## nebulactrl domains

Manage service domains.

```
nebulactrl domains
```

### nebulactrl domains add

Attach a hostname to a service.

```
nebulactrl domains add <service> <hostname> [flags]
```

Options:

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--component` | string |  | Compose stacks: the component (compose service) the domain routes to |
| `--port` | int |  | target port (default: the service port; Compose stacks: the container port, optional when the component declares one) |
| `--process` | string |  | services with several processes: the process the domain routes to (default: the default process, or the only one with a port); the target port is the process' port |
| `--www-redirect` | bool |  | also route the www/apex counterpart and 301-redirect it to this hostname (needs proxy:write; both hostnames get certificates) |

### nebulactrl domains generate

Generate a domain from the server's base domain.

```
nebulactrl domains generate <service> [flags]
```

Options:

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--component` | string |  | Compose stacks: the component the generated domain routes to |
| `--process` | string |  | services with several processes: the process the generated domain routes to |

### nebulactrl domains ls

List a service's domains.

```
nebulactrl domains ls <service>
```

### nebulactrl domains rm

Remove a domain from a service.

```
nebulactrl domains rm <service> <hostname|domain-id>
```

### nebulactrl domains www

Turn the www/apex redirect of a domain on or off.

```
nebulactrl domains www <service> <hostname|domain-id> <on|off>
```

`on` routes the www/apex counterpart of the domain (www.<host>, or the host without its www.) and answers it with
a 301 redirect to the domain, keeping the path and query. Both hostnames get certificates and each needs its own
DNS record. `off` removes the redirect. The change is staged until the next deploy. Needs proxy:write; the domain
must be a whole-host serve domain without a path prefix.

Examples:

```sh
nebulactrl domains www acme/production/web example.com on
```

## nebulactrl envs

Manage environments.

```
nebulactrl envs
```

### nebulactrl envs clone

Clone an environment into a new, non-production one.

```
nebulactrl envs clone <env> --project <project> --name <name> [--domains drop|suffix] [--dry-run] [flags]
```

Create a new environment with a staged copy of every service of <env>: configuration, variables, the environment's shared variables, volume definitions, links and the canvas layout. Slugs are kept, so ${{postgres.DATABASE_URL}} in a cloned service points at the cloned postgres. Secrets are copied sealed and generated values are generated again. Databases are new and empty (restore a dump into them); volumes are new and empty. Nothing runs until the services are deployed.

Options:

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--domain-suffix` | string |  | suffix for --domains suffix (default: -copy in the same environment, -<environment slug> otherwise) |
| `--domains` | string | `drop` | domains of the clone: drop (attach new ones later) or suffix (suffix the first label of each hostname) |
| `--dry-run` | bool |  | show what the clone would do and change nothing |
| `--name` | string |  | name of the new environment |
| `--project` | string |  | project ID, slug or name |
| `--server` | string |  | place the clone on this server (ID or name; default: the source's server) |

### nebulactrl envs ls

List the environments of a project.

```
nebulactrl envs ls --project <project> [flags]
```

Options:

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--project` | string |  | project ID, slug or name |

## nebulactrl import

Import a project from another tool.

```
nebulactrl import
```

### nebulactrl import compose

Import a Docker Compose project as staged services.

```
nebulactrl import compose <docker-compose.yml|-> --project <p> --env <e> --server <s> [flags]
```

Reads a Compose file (a local file, stdin with -, or a file in a git repository with --repo) and stages one NebulaCtrl service per
Compose service in the environment, grouped on the canvas and linked in deploy order. Nothing is deployed unless you pass --deploy.

Files next to the Compose file (.env, env_file entries, bind-mounted config files) are read from disk. Host names of other
services in variables are rewritten to references, and official database images become managed databases unless you turn that off.
Use --plan to review without changing anything. Per-service decisions are written as <service>=<value> or <service>.<KEY>.

With --as-stack the whole file becomes ONE service (a native Compose stack): the file is kept as written, the .env entries become the
stack's variables (used for ${VAR} interpolation only), and domains are suggested per component. A stack runs under the safe
allow-list (no privileged mode, host network, devices, Docker socket or host bind mounts, no build:) unless an instance admin made
the server unrestricted; violations are listed and block the import. In stack mode --secret, --not-secret and
--skip-var take the variable name (<KEY>); --domain and --port take the component name.

Options:

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--as-stack` | bool |  | run the whole file as one native Compose stack (one service, the file kept as written) instead of splitting it into services |
| `--branch` | string |  | branch of --repo or --repo-url (default: the default branch) |
| `--connection` | string |  | git connection ID or name for --repo |
| `--convert-bind` | stringArray |  | <service>=<container path>: turn a directory bind mount into a named volume (repeatable) |
| `--deploy` | bool |  | deploy the new services right away |
| `--domain` | stringArray |  | <service>=<hostname>\|auto\|off: set the domain (repeatable) |
| `--env` | string |  | environment ID, slug or name |
| `--env-file` | string |  | the .env file for ${VAR} interpolation (default: .env next to the Compose file) |
| `--exclude` | stringArray |  | <service>: do not import this service (repeatable) |
| `--file` | stringArray |  | supply a referenced file: <path as written in Compose>=<local file> (repeatable) |
| `--git` | stringArray |  | <service>=<https url>[#branch]: build a service from this repository (repeatable) |
| `--image` | stringArray |  | <service>=<image>: pull this image instead of building (repeatable) |
| `--include` | stringArray |  | <service>: also import a service that Compose gates behind a profile (repeatable) |
| `--managed` | stringArray |  | <service>: use a managed database (repeatable; needed to accept the licence of Redis and MongoDB) |
| `--name` | string |  | canvas group title (default: the Compose project name) |
| `--no-managed` | stringArray |  | <service>: keep an official database image as a plain image service (repeatable) |
| `--no-rewrite` | stringArray |  | <service>.<KEY>: keep the host names in the variable as they are (repeatable) |
| `--not-secret` | stringArray |  | <service>.<KEY>: store the variable in plain text (repeatable) |
| `--path` | string |  | path of the Compose file in the repository (default: docker-compose.yml, compose.yaml, ...) |
| `--plan` | bool |  | show what would be imported and change nothing |
| `--port` | stringArray |  | <service>=<port>: the service port (repeatable) |
| `--project` | string |  | project ID, slug or name |
| `--publish` | stringArray |  | <service>=<port>/<tcp\|udp>: publish a container port through a TCP/UDP route (repeatable) |
| `--repo` | string |  | read the Compose file from owner/name of a git connection (with --connection) |
| `--repo-url` | string |  | read the Compose file from a public github.com or gitlab.com repository URL |
| `--secret` | stringArray |  | <service>.<KEY>: store the variable as a secret (repeatable) |
| `--server` | string |  | server ID or name the services run on |
| `--skip-var` | stringArray |  | <service>.<KEY>: do not import the variable (repeatable) |

### nebulactrl import coolify

Import projects, applications and databases from a Coolify v4 instance as staged services.

```
nebulactrl import coolify --url <coolify url> --server <server> [flags]
```

Reads a Coolify instance through its API and stages the same projects and environments here: applications become image or git services
(Dockerfile builds stay Dockerfile builds, Nixpacks becomes Railpack), databases become managed databases of the same engine and version,
domains, health checks, resource limits, custom Docker options, deployment commands and variables come along. Variables that point at a Coolify
database or application are rewritten to ${{service.EXPORT}} references; credentials, locked values and secret-looking keys are stored as secrets.
Nothing is deployed unless you pass --deploy, and database and volume DATA is never copied (the plan prints the follow-up commands).

The Coolify API token needs the `read` and `read:sensitive` abilities (Keys & Tokens → API tokens in Coolify); read:sensitive is what returns
variable values and custom Docker options. The token is read from --token-env (default COOLIFY_TOKEN), --token-file or --token, sent to your
NebulaCtrl server for this one request, and never stored or printed. Registry pull credentials cannot be read from Coolify: give them with
--registry-user and --registry-token-env.

Use --plan (or --dry-run) to review without changing anything: it lists every resource, its variables by key (never values), the rewritten
references and everything that is not imported. Per-resource decisions name the resource by its Coolify name or UUID, variables as <resource>.<KEY>.

Options:

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--deploy` | bool |  | deploy the new services right away (default: everything stays staged) |
| `--domain` | stringArray |  | <resource>/<coolify host>=<new host>\|off: change or drop a domain (repeatable) |
| `--dry-run` | bool |  | same as --plan |
| `--engine-version` | stringArray |  | <database>=<version>: managed database version (repeatable) |
| `--exclude` | stringArray |  | <resource>: do not import this application or database (repeatable) |
| `--git-connection` | string |  | git connection ID or name used to clone private GitHub/GitLab repositories |
| `--include` | stringArray |  | <resource>: import it although it is off by default; for Redis and MongoDB this accepts their source-available licence (repeatable) |
| `--into` | stringArray |  | <coolify project>=<project>: import into an existing project instead of creating one (repeatable) |
| `--kind` | stringArray |  | <resource>=<app\|worker> (repeatable) |
| `--no-rewrite` | stringArray |  | <resource>.<KEY>: keep host names and credentials of Coolify resources in the value as they are (repeatable) |
| `--not-secret` | stringArray |  | <resource>.<KEY>: store the variable in plain text (repeatable) |
| `--plan` | bool |  | show what would be imported and change nothing |
| `--port` | stringArray |  | <resource>=<port>: service port; 0 makes it a worker without a port (repeatable) |
| `--registry-token-env` | stringArray |  | <registry host>=<ENV_VAR>: environment variable with that registry's token or password (repeatable) |
| `--registry-user` | stringArray |  | <registry host>=<username>: pull credential user, for example ghcr.io=octocat (repeatable) |
| `--rename` | stringArray |  | <resource>=<name>: service name (repeatable) |
| `--rename-project` | stringArray |  | <coolify project>=<name>: name of the new project (default: the same name, plus " (Coolify)" when it exists) |
| `--secret` | stringArray |  | <resource>.<KEY>: store the variable as a secret (repeatable) |
| `--server` | string |  | server ID or name the services run on (required to import) |
| `--set` | stringArray |  | <resource>.<KEY>=<value>: supply the value of a locked variable (visible in the process list: prefer --set-env) (repeatable) |
| `--set-env` | stringArray |  | <resource>.<KEY>=<ENV_VAR>: supply the value of a locked variable from an environment variable (repeatable) |
| `--skip-project` | stringArray |  | <coolify project>: do not import this project (repeatable) |
| `--skip-var` | stringArray |  | <resource>.<KEY>: do not import the variable (repeatable) |
| `--token` | string |  | Coolify API token (visible in the process list: prefer --token-env or --token-file) |
| `--token-env` | string | `COOLIFY_TOKEN` | environment variable that holds the Coolify API token |
| `--token-file` | string |  | read the Coolify API token from this file (- for stdin) |
| `--url` | string |  | address of the Coolify instance (default: $COOLIFY_URL) |

## nebulactrl instance

Settings of the whole installation (instance admin only).

```
nebulactrl instance
```

### nebulactrl instance dashboard-access

Who may reach the dashboard and how its certificate is issued.

```
nebulactrl instance dashboard-access
```

#### nebulactrl instance dashboard-access get

Show the dashboard's allow list and certificate method.

```
nebulactrl instance dashboard-access get
```

#### nebulactrl instance dashboard-access set

Change the dashboard's allow list and certificate method.

```
nebulactrl instance dashboard-access set [--allow <cidr>]... [--tailnet-only | --clear-allow] [--dns-resolver <provider> | --http-01] [--confirm-lockout] [flags]
```

Restricts who may reach the dashboard's hostname (an IP allow list on its route) and chooses how its certificate is issued.
Settings you do not name stay as they are. --allow replaces the list (repeat it or separate CIDRs with commas; IPv4 and IPv6).
--tailnet-only is the list 100.64.0.0/10, fd7a:115c:a1e0::/48. Agents on other servers and webhooks reach the control plane
through the same hostname, so keep their addresses in the list.
The change is refused (409 dashboard_lockout) when the list leaves out the address you are connecting from, unless --confirm-lockout is set.
--dns-resolver needs a resolver of that provider on the control-plane server (Servers, Proxy). Run from the host with an SSH tunnel to recover from a lock-out.

Options:

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--allow` | stringSlice |  | CIDR or address allowed to reach the dashboard; replaces the list (repeatable, comma separated) |
| `--clear-allow` | bool |  | lift the restriction: everybody may reach the dashboard |
| `--confirm-lockout` | bool |  | save even though the list excludes the address you are connecting from |
| `--dns-resolver` | string |  | issue the certificate through this DNS-01 provider (for example cloudflare) |
| `--http-01` | bool |  | issue the certificate automatically over HTTP-01 |
| `--tailnet-only` | bool |  | allow only Tailscale addresses (100.64.0.0/10, fd7a:115c:a1e0::/48) |

## nebulactrl login

Store the control plane URL and API token.

```
nebulactrl login --url <url> --token <token> [flags]
```

Verifies the token against GET /me and writes ~/.config/nebulactrl/config.json (mode 0600).
Pass --token - to read the token from stdin; NEBULACTRL_TOKEN is used when --token is omitted.
The token travels with every command, so the URL must be https://. Plain http is accepted for this machine only, or elsewhere with --insecure.
Use a REST API token (Account → API tokens); an MCP token is for agents and is refused here.

Options:

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--token` | string |  | API token (nct_…); - reads stdin |
| `--url` | string |  | control plane URL, e.g. https://nebula.example.com |

### nebulactrl mesh enable

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |

| `--accept-mesh-changes` | bool |  | confirm that this adds tailnet devices |

### nebulactrl mesh reconcile

```

Mode add creates every link the environment's variable references and canvas links need. It adds tailnet devices (tagged devices may be billed by Tailscale), so it needs --accept-mesh-changes.
Mode repair only removes grants whose source is gone; it never adds a device.

Options:

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--accept-mesh-changes` | bool |  | confirm the tailnet devices mode add creates |

```

The placement is replaced as a unit: --build-server pins a build server and --registry names the registry; an
