## nebulactrl servers

Manage Docker hosts.

```
nebulactrl servers
```

### nebulactrl servers enroll-token

Create a one-time agent enrollment token.

```
nebulactrl servers enroll-token --name <name> [flags]
```

Registers a pending server and prints the one-hour, single-use enrollment token together with the
command that installs the agent on the host. The token is shown once.

Options:

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--acme-email` | string |  | email for Let's Encrypt registration |
| `--base-domain` | string |  | base domain for generated hostnames |
| `--name` | string |  | server name |
| `--public-ip` | string |  | public IP, used for DNS checks and sslip.io domains |

### nebulactrl servers ls

List servers.

```
nebulactrl servers ls
```

### nebulactrl servers revoke

Revoke a server's agent identity.

```
nebulactrl servers revoke <server-id|name>
```

Disconnects the agent and cancels its pending commands. The agent must re-enroll to come back.

### nebulactrl servers unrestricted

Show, enable or disable the Unrestricted switch of a server (instance admin).

```
nebulactrl servers unrestricted <server-id|name> [--on --confirm <name> | --off] [flags]
```

By default Compose stacks and services run under safe allow-lists. An unrestricted server lifts them for everything on it:
privileged mode, host networking, devices, GPUs, a custom runtime, the host PID namespace, unconfined seccomp or AppArmor,
NET_ADMIN, SYS_ADMIN, the Docker socket and host bind mounts. Anyone who can deploy there can take over the server, so only
the instance admin can switch it, and enabling needs --confirm with the server's exact name. Disabling does not stop running
containers; the next deploy of something that needs it fails. Without --on or --off, prints the current state.

Options:

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--confirm` | string |  | the server's exact name (required with --on) |
| `--off` | bool |  | make the server restricted again |
| `--on` | bool |  | make the server unrestricted |

### nebulactrl servers update

Set a server's role and build settings.

```
nebulactrl servers update <server-id|name> [--role deployments|builds|both] [--max-builds <n>] [--allow-emulation[=false]] [--allow-previews[=false]] [flags]
```

Roles: `deployments` runs services (the default), `builds` only builds images for other servers and pushes them
to a registry, `both` does both. A build server needs an agent that can build and push (`build.push`).
--max-builds caps parallel builds (1-16, default 2; more queue). --allow-emulation lets it build for another
CPU architecture (slow). --allow-previews lets pull request previews build on it (off: previews build on their own server).

Options:

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--allow-emulation` | bool |  | allow cross-architecture builds through emulation |
| `--allow-previews` | bool |  | let pull request previews build here |
| `--max-builds` | int |  | parallel builds on this server (1-16) |
| `--role` | string |  | deployments, builds or both |

## nebulactrl services

Manage services.

```
nebulactrl services
```

### nebulactrl services build-plan

Preview how a git service would be built.

```
nebulactrl services build-plan <service>
```

Asks the service's server to clone the branch head and report the build method (Dockerfile, Railpack or a
starter Dockerfile), the detected providers and the start command. Nothing is built or deployed.

### nebulactrl services clone

Clone a service (staged copy; secrets are copied sealed).

```
nebulactrl services clone <service> [--env <env> [--project <project>]] [--name <name>] [--domains drop|suffix] [--dry-run] [flags]
```

Clone a service into the same or another environment. The clone is staged: nothing runs until it is deployed.

It gets the configuration, variables (secrets stay secret, generated values are generated again), volume definitions (new, empty volumes) and, in the same environment, the source's links. A managed database is created new and empty: restore a dump into it. Domains are dropped by default or cloned with a suffix.

Options:

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--domain-suffix` | string |  | suffix for --domains suffix (default: -copy in the same environment, -<environment slug> otherwise) |
| `--domains` | string | `drop` | domains of the clone: drop (attach new ones later) or suffix (suffix the first label of each hostname) |
| `--dry-run` | bool |  | show what the clone would do and change nothing |
| `--env` | string |  | environment of the clone (ID, slug or name; default: the source's environment) |
| `--name` | string |  | name of the clone (default: "<name> copy" in the same environment) |
| `--project` | string |  | project of --env (default: the source's project) |
| `--server` | string |  | place the clone on this server (ID or name; default: the source's server) |

### nebulactrl services combine

Merge several services into one service with a process each.

```
nebulactrl services combine <service>... [--into <target>] [--process-name <service>=<name>]... [--var KEY=<service>]... [--stop-sources-first] [--yes] [--wait] [flags]
```

Merges git services of one environment that share a repository and build settings into one service. The target (--into;
default: the service with the most domains) keeps running and gains one process per other service, with that service's
start command, port, health check, limits and replicas. They share the target's one build, image, variables and release.

Without --yes this only prints the plan: what blocks the merge, which variables differ, which domains and tasks move.
With --yes it stages the target, deploys it once (all processes, all or nothing) and, only when that succeeded, moves the
other services' domains and scheduled tasks to the target and deletes those services (their volumes are kept). If the
deployment fails nothing was deleted: retry or abort with `services combine retry|abort <combine-id>`. After the merge
is done there is no way back.

A variable that the services set to different values must be chosen: --var KEY=<service> keeps that service's value.
Every other service becomes a process named after its slug (--process-name <service>=<name> changes it; naming the
target renames its own process, default web). --stop-sources-first stops services without domains before the deployment,
so a worker or scheduler never runs twice at the same time.

Examples:

```sh
nebulactrl services combine acme/production/worker acme/production/scheduler --into acme/production/web
  nebulactrl services combine worker --into web --var APP_ENV=web --process-name worker=queue --yes --wait
```

Options:

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--into` | string |  | the service that keeps running and gains the others as processes |
| `--process-name` | stringArray |  | process name of a service: <service>=<name> (the target's own process too) |
| `--stop-sources-first` | bool |  | stop the services without domains before the deployment |
| `--timeout` | duration | `30m0s` | give up waiting after this long (with --wait) |
| `--var` | stringArray |  | for a variable that differs between the services: KEY=<service> keeps that service's value |
| `--wait` | bool |  | wait until the merge is done; exit non-zero if it failed |
| `--yes` | bool |  | start the merge (without it the plan is only printed) |

#### nebulactrl services combine abort

Take back a staged or failed combine.

```
nebulactrl services combine abort <combine-id>
```

Restarts the services the combine stopped, discards what it staged on the target and removes the scale settings it
created. Not possible while the deployment or the cutover runs, and not once the services are merged.

#### nebulactrl services combine retry

Run a failed combine again.

```
nebulactrl services combine retry <combine-id> [--wait] [flags]
```

Deploys the target again with the configuration the combine staged, then moves the domains and tasks and deletes the
other services. When the target already runs every process only that last step runs.

Options:

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--timeout` | duration | `30m0s` | give up waiting after this long (with --wait) |
| `--wait` | bool |  | wait until the merge is done; exit non-zero if it failed |

#### nebulactrl services combine status

Show the state of a combine.

```
nebulactrl services combine status <combine-id>
```

### nebulactrl services create

Create a service (staged until deployed).

```
nebulactrl services create --project <project> --env <env> --name <name> (--image <ref> | --git <url> [--branch <b>]) [--server <server>] [--port <n>] [flags]
```

Options:

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--branch` | string |  | Git branch (default: the repository default) |
| `--build-location` | string |  | where the git source is built: inherit (default), target or build-server |
| `--build-server` | string |  | pin the build server (ID or name); with --build-location build-server |
| `--build-type` | string |  | how a git source is built: auto (default), dockerfile, railpack or starter:<node\|python\|go\|ruby\|php\|static> |
| `--env` | string |  | environment ID, slug or name |
| `--git` | string |  | Git repository URL (built on the target server, or on a build server) |
| `--image` | string |  | Docker image, e.g. traefik/whoami:latest |
| `--name` | string |  | service name |
| `--port` | int |  | HTTP/internal port the service listens on (0 = none) |
| `--project` | string |  | project ID, slug or name |
| `--registry` | string |  | registry ID the build is pushed to (default: the project or team registry) |
| `--server` | string |  | target server ID or name |

### nebulactrl services deploy

Deploy a service.

```
nebulactrl services deploy <service> [flags]
```

Starts a deployment and returns once it is accepted (HTTP 202). With --wait, polls until the
deployment reaches a terminal status and exits 0 only when it is `succeeded`.
With --no-cache a git service builds this one deployment without any cache (docker build --no-cache --pull,
no reuse of an image a build server already pushed); later deployments build normally.

Options:

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--no-cache` | bool |  | build this deployment without cache (git services; docker build --no-cache --pull) |
| `--timeout` | duration | `30m0s` | give up waiting after this long (with --wait) |
| `--wait` | bool |  | wait for the deployment to finish; exit non-zero unless it succeeded |

### nebulactrl services deploy-hook

Show, enable, disable or rotate a service's deploy hook.

```
nebulactrl services deploy-hook <service> [--enable|--disable|--rotate] [flags]
```

A deploy hook is a URL (POST /hooks/deploy/<service-id>/<secret>) that deploys the service like a manual deploy,
for CI pipelines and container registries (Docker Hub, GHCR). Without a flag the command shows the hook's state.

--enable creates a secret and prints the URL; --rotate replaces the secret of an enabled hook and prints the new URL;
--disable turns the hook off and deletes the secret. The URL is shown once and cannot be read again.
Managing a hook needs the deployments:write scope.

Options:

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--disable` | bool |  | turn the hook off and delete its secret |
| `--enable` | bool |  | turn the hook on with a new secret and print the URL once |
| `--rotate` | bool |  | replace the secret of an enabled hook and print the new URL once |

### nebulactrl services docker

Show or set a service's Docker options (staged until the next deployment).

```
nebulactrl services docker <service> [flags]
```

Without flags, prints the service's Docker options. With flags, changes them and stages the service. The options are typed:
there is no free-text docker run string. Hardening options (--cap-drop ALL, --no-new-privileges, --read-only, --pids-limit),
--hostname, --dns, curated --sysctl, --user and --group-add work on every server.

--device, --gpus, --runtime, --privileged, --pid-host, --seccomp-unconfined, --apparmor-unconfined (and the NET_ADMIN and
SYS_ADMIN capabilities, set in the web UI) work only on a server an instance admin made unrestricted
(`nebulactrl servers unrestricted`): they can hand over the host. Other servers answer 422 requires_unrestricted_server.
Capabilities to add, ulimits, shm size, extra hosts, labels, tmpfs and the entrypoint are edited in the web UI.

Options:

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--apparmor-unconfined` | bool |  | [unrestricted server] run without the default AppArmor profile |
| `--cap-drop` | stringSlice |  | capabilities to drop, e.g. ALL or NET_RAW (comma-separated; none clears) |
| `--clear` | bool |  | remove every Docker option of the service |
| `--device` | stringArray |  | [unrestricted server] host device host[:container][:perms], repeatable; none clears |
| `--dns` | stringSlice |  | DNS resolver IPs, at most 3 (none clears) |
| `--gpus` | string |  | [unrestricted server] NVIDIA GPUs: all or a count (none clears) |
| `--group-add` | stringSlice |  | supplementary numeric group IDs (none clears) |
| `--hostname` | string |  | container hostname (default: the service slug; "default" resets) |
| `--no-new-privileges` | bool |  | set the no-new-privileges security option (--no-new-privileges=false turns it off) |
| `--pid-host` | bool |  | [unrestricted server] share the host's PID namespace |
| `--pids-limit` | int64 |  | limit the processes and threads of the container (0 = no limit) |
| `--privileged` | bool |  | [unrestricted server] privileged mode: root on the host |
| `--read-only` | bool |  | mount the root filesystem read-only (config files must then sit on a volume) |
| `--runtime` | string |  | [unrestricted server] OCI runtime, e.g. runsc (default resets) |
| `--seccomp-unconfined` | bool |  | [unrestricted server] run without the default seccomp profile |
| `--sysctl` | stringArray |  | namespaced kernel parameter key=value, repeatable (key= removes it) |
| `--user` | string |  | run as uid[:gid] ("default" resets to the image's user) |

### nebulactrl services download-logs

Download a service's stored runtime logs as a file.

```
nebulactrl services download-logs <service> [flags]
```

Writes the service's stored runtime log (the server keeps 7 days by default), oldest first, as plain text
(`<time> <line>`) or NDJSON. Secret values are masked on the server. At most 200,000 lines: a longer range
ends with a note, so narrow it with --from/--to. Needs the logs:read scope and the service's server online.

Examples:

```sh
nebulactrl services download-logs acme/production/web --from 24h -o web.log
  nebulactrl services download-logs web --format ndjson --grep 'level:error' > errors.ndjson
```

Options:

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--component` | string |  | Compose stacks: only this component's lines |
| `--format` | string | `txt` | file format: txt or ndjson |
| `--from` | string |  | only lines at or after this time: RFC 3339, a date, or a duration ago (24h) |
| `--grep` | string |  | only lines matching this log search query (free text, "phrases", level:error) |
| `-o, --output` | string |  | write to this file instead of stdout (created with mode 0600) |
| `--process` | string |  | services with several processes: only this process' lines (default: every process) |
| `--to` | string |  | only lines before this time (same forms as --from) |

### nebulactrl services logs

Show runtime logs of a service.

```
nebulactrl services logs <service> [--process <name>] [flags]
```

Options:

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `-f, --follow` | bool |  | stream new lines until interrupted |
| `--process` | string |  | services with several processes: only this process' lines (default: every process, each line prefixed '<process> \| ') |
| `--tail` | int | `200` | number of recent lines to show |
| `--timestamps` | bool |  | prefix each line with its timestamp |

### nebulactrl services ls

List the services of an environment.

```
nebulactrl services ls --project <project> --env <env> [flags]
```

Options:

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--env` | string |  | environment ID, slug or name |
| `--project` | string |  | project ID, slug or name |

### nebulactrl services maintenance

Put a service into maintenance mode, or take it out.

```
nebulactrl services maintenance <service> on|off [--title <t>] [--message <m>] [--eta <rfc3339|duration>] [flags]
```

While on, every domain of the service answers HTTP 503 with a maintenance page and a Retry-After header instead of
reaching the service. It takes effect immediately without a deployment, and it is never staged or rolled back.
--eta takes an RFC 3339 time (2026-11-02T09:30:00Z) or a duration from now (45m, 2h). The page text and ETA are
only used with `on`; `off` keeps the stored text for next time.

Options:

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--eta` | string |  | expected return: an RFC 3339 time or a duration from now (45m, 2h) |
| `--message` | string |  | page message |
| `--title` | string |  | page title (default: Down for maintenance) |

### nebulactrl services move

Move a service to another environment (staged until the next deploy).

```
nebulactrl services move <service> --env <env> [--project <project>] [--force] [--dry-run] [flags]
```

Move a service to another environment. It keeps running where it is until its next deployment, which joins the new environment's network and variables. References are checked first: variables that point at services staying behind, and other services' variables that point at the moved one, break. Without --force a move that breaks references is refused; --dry-run prints the plan. Canvas links of the service are removed.

Options:

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--dry-run` | bool |  | print the plan (references, links, slug) and change nothing |
| `--env` | string |  | target environment (ID, slug or name) |
| `--force` | bool |  | move even though references from or to the service break |
| `--project` | string |  | project of --env (default: the service's project) |

### nebulactrl services processes

Manage the processes of a service.

```
nebulactrl services processes
```

A service has a default process (its own port, start command and health check, named web unless set otherwise)
and any number of named processes (a queue worker, a scheduler) that run the same image with their own command.
They share one build, one set of variables and one release. Adding, changing and removing a process is staged
until the next deployment; replicas and autoscaling apply immediately.

#### nebulactrl services processes ls

List the processes of a service.

```
nebulactrl services processes ls <service>
```

#### nebulactrl services processes rename

Rename a process (staged until the next deployment).

```
nebulactrl services processes rename <service> <old> <new>
```

Renames a process and keeps its replica setting and its domains. The default process is renamed too. A renamed
process is a new set of containers: the old ones stop at the next deployment.

#### nebulactrl services processes rm

Remove a process (staged until the next deployment).

```
nebulactrl services processes rm <service> <name>
```

Removes a named process from the service's configuration. The running process stops at the next deployment.
A process that still has a domain cannot be removed: remove the domain first. The default process is the service
itself and cannot be removed.

#### nebulactrl services processes scale

Set the replicas or autoscaling of one process.

```
nebulactrl services processes scale <service> <name> [<replicas>] [--autoscale min:max[:target]|off] [flags]
```

Like `services scale`, for one process: runs it on 1-10 replicas, or scales it on CPU. The change applies
immediately without a deployment. A process with volumes or files on the service, or a singleton, runs one instance.

Options:

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--autoscale` | string |  | autoscale on CPU between min and max replicas: min:max[:target%] or off |

#### nebulactrl services processes set

Add a process or change one (staged until the next deployment).

```
nebulactrl services processes set <service> [<name>] [--command ARG... | --command-json '[...]'] [--port N] [--stop-grace-seconds N] [--singleton[=false]] [--memory-mb N] [--cpus F] [--health-type ...] [--default] [--name NEW] [flags]
```

Adds the process <name> when the service has none of that name (a command is required), otherwise changes the
settings you give and keeps the rest. The command is an argv list, no shell: repeat --command per element, give
--command-json '["bin/rails","sidekiq"]', or put it after `--`.

--default (or the default process' own name) edits the service's own process: its command, port, health check,
stop grace, limits and singleton flag. --name renames the default process. Other processes are renamed with
`processes rename`. Singleton: never two instances at once; the old one stops before the new one starts.

Examples:

```sh
nebulactrl services processes set acme/production/web worker --command bundle --command exec --command sidekiq --stop-grace-seconds 120
  nebulactrl services processes set web scheduler --singleton -- php artisan schedule:work
  nebulactrl services processes set web --default --port 3000
```

Options:

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--command` | stringArray |  | start command, one element per flag (argv, no shell) |
| `--command-json` | string |  | start command as a JSON array of strings |
| `--cpus` | float64 |  | CPU limit (0: the service's limit) |
| `--default` | bool |  | edit the service's own (default) process |
| `--health-command` | stringArray |  | exec health check command, repeat per argument (CMD or CMD-SHELL first) |
| `--health-deadline` | int |  | seconds the process has to become healthy |
| `--health-interval` | int |  | seconds between health checks |
| `--health-path` | string |  | health check HTTP path |
| `--health-port` | int |  | health check port (default: the process' port) |
| `--health-start-period` | int |  | seconds after start during which failures do not count |
| `--health-success-threshold` | int |  | consecutive successes that make the process healthy |
| `--health-timeout` | int |  | seconds one health check may take |
| `--health-type` | string |  | health check: none, http, tcp or exec |
| `--memory-mb` | int |  | memory limit in MB (0: the service's limit) |
| `--name` | string |  | with --default: rename the default process |
| `--port` | int |  | HTTP port the process listens on (0: none); unique across the service's processes |
| `--singleton` | bool |  | never run two instances at once (--singleton=false to allow it) |
| `--stop-grace-seconds` | int |  | seconds between the stop signal and the kill (0: the service's value) |

### nebulactrl services restart

Restart a service's container.

```
nebulactrl services restart <service>
```

### nebulactrl services run

Run a one-off command in a container of the service's image.

```
nebulactrl services run <service> -- <command...> [flags]
```

Runs the command (argv, no shell; use `-- sh -c '...'` for shell syntax) in a throwaway container of the service's
current image, with its environment, networks and resource limits, on its server. Prints the output and exits
with the command's exit code. Needs the deployments:write scope and is audited.

Options:

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--detach` | bool |  | start the run and return without waiting for it |
| `--timeout` | duration | `0s` | stop the command after this long (default 30m) |

### nebulactrl services scale

Set the number of replicas or turn on autoscaling.

```
nebulactrl services scale <service> [<replicas>] [--autoscale min:max[:target]|off] [--process <name>] [flags]
```

Runs a stateless service (no volumes, an HTTP port) on 1-10 replicas on its server. The change applies
immediately without a deployment and without a rebuild. --autoscale min:max[:target] scales on CPU
(target percent of the replica's CPU limit, default 70); --autoscale off returns to manual scaling.
A service with several processes scales its default process; --process <name> scales another one
(the same as `services processes scale`).

Options:

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--autoscale` | string |  | autoscale on CPU between min and max replicas: min:max[:target%] or off |
| `--process` | string |  | services with several processes: the process to scale (default: the default process) |

### nebulactrl services shell

Open an interactive shell in a service's container.

```
nebulactrl services shell <service> [-- command args…] [flags]
```

Opens a terminal in a running replica of the service (bash if the image has it, else sh), or runs the command after `--` with a terminal attached. Needs the Owner, Admin or Developer role and a token with deployments:write. Production services need --production. Sessions are audited (never their input or output) and close after 15 minutes without input.

Examples:

```sh
nebulactrl services shell acme/production/web
  nebulactrl services shell web --replica 1 -- psql -U postgres
  nebulactrl services shell web --process worker
```

Options:

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--process` | string |  | services with several processes: the process to open (default: the default process); --replica counts within it |
| `--production` | bool |  | confirm opening a terminal in a production environment |
| `--replica` | int |  | replica index to open (0-based) |

### nebulactrl services update

Set where and how a service is built.

```
nebulactrl services update <service> [--build-location inherit|target|build-server] [--build-server <server|none>] [--registry <id|none>] [--submodules auto|on|off] [flags]
```

The service's own override of the project and team build settings; `inherit` follows them. `none` clears a pin or
registry. `--submodules` sets the git submodule checkout (auto: recursive when the repository has a .gitmodules file; on: always, a failure fails the build; off). The change is staged until the next deployment, like every setting. Compose stacks are edited in the web UI.

Options:

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--build-location` | string |  | inherit, target or build-server |
| `--build-server` | string |  | pin the build server (ID or name; none clears) |
| `--registry` | string |  | registry ID (none clears) |
| `--submodules` | string |  | git submodules: auto, on or off |

## nebulactrl tasks

Cron tasks and their runs.

```
nebulactrl tasks
```

### nebulactrl tasks create

Schedule a recurring command.

```
nebulactrl tasks create <service> --name <name> --schedule <cron> -- <command...> [flags]
```

Runs the command (argv, no shell; use `-- sh -c '...'` for shell syntax) in a throwaway container of the service's
current image with its environment. The schedule is a 5-field cron expression or @hourly/@daily/@weekly/@monthly,
evaluated in --timezone (an IANA name such as Europe/Berlin; default UTC). Daylight-saving changes keep the wall-clock
time: a run in the skipped hour is skipped for that day, a repeated hour runs once.

Options:

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--concurrency` | string |  | forbid (default: skip a tick while the previous run is active) or allow |
| `--disabled` | bool |  | create the task disabled |
| `--name` | string |  | task name, unique per service |
| `--schedule` | string |  | cron expression, e.g. "*/15 * * * *" or @daily, evaluated in --timezone |
| `--timeout` | duration | `0s` | stop a run after this long (default 30m) |
| `--timezone` | string |  | IANA time zone of the schedule, e.g. Europe/Berlin (default UTC) |

### nebulactrl tasks logs

Print the output of a run (follows a run that is still active).

```
nebulactrl tasks logs <run-id>
```

### nebulactrl tasks ls

List a service's cron tasks.

```
nebulactrl tasks ls <service>
```

### nebulactrl tasks rm

Delete a cron task and its run history.

```
nebulactrl tasks rm <service> <task>
```

### nebulactrl tasks run

Run a cron task now and follow its output.

```
nebulactrl tasks run <service> <task> [flags]
```

Starts a run immediately (whatever the schedule), prints its output and exits with the command's exit code.

Options:

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--detach` | bool |  | start the run and return without waiting for it |

### nebulactrl tasks runs

Run history of a service's tasks and one-off commands.

```
nebulactrl tasks runs <service> [flags]
```

Options:

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--limit` | int |  | how many runs (default 50) |
| `--task` | string |  | only the runs of this task (name or id) |

### nebulactrl tasks update

Change a cron task's schedule, time zone or whether it runs.

```
nebulactrl tasks update <service> <task> [--schedule <cron>] [--timezone <zone>] [--enable|--disable] [flags]
```

Changing the schedule or the time zone recomputes the next run from now; the new next run is printed.
The time zone is an IANA name such as Europe/Berlin (UTC when never set).

--disable stops the schedule from starting runs and keeps the task, its history and its settings; --enable starts it again.
Give at most one of them.

Examples:

```sh
nebulactrl tasks update acme/production/web nightly --timezone Europe/Berlin
  nebulactrl tasks update acme/production/web nightly --disable
```

Options:

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--disable` | bool |  | turn the task off; it is kept and does not run on schedule |
| `--enable` | bool |  | turn the task on, so its schedule starts runs |
| `--schedule` | string |  | new cron expression |
| `--timezone` | string |  | new IANA time zone |

## nebulactrl teams

Manage teams.

```
nebulactrl teams
```

### nebulactrl teams create

Create a team (you become its owner; needs an admin-scope token).

```
nebulactrl teams create <name>
```

### nebulactrl teams ls

List your teams and the saved token per team.

```
nebulactrl teams ls
```

### nebulactrl teams switch

Use the saved token of another team.

```
nebulactrl teams switch <slug>
```

## nebulactrl templates

Browse and install one-click templates.

```
nebulactrl templates
```

### nebulactrl templates install

Install a template as staged services (or deploy right away).

```
nebulactrl templates install <template> --project <p> --env <e> --server <s> [--input KEY=VALUE]... [--deploy] [flags]
```

Options:

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--deploy` | bool |  | deploy the new services right away |
| `--env` | string |  | environment ID, slug or name |
| `--input` | stringArray |  | install input KEY=VALUE (repeatable) |
| `--name` | string |  | canvas group title |
| `--project` | string |  | project ID, slug or name |
| `--server` | string |  | server ID or name the stack runs on |

### nebulactrl templates installed

List the template stacks of an environment.

```
nebulactrl templates installed --project <p> --env <e> [flags]
```

Options:

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--env` | string |  | environment ID, slug or name |
| `--project` | string |  | project ID, slug or name |

### nebulactrl templates ls

List catalog templates.

```
nebulactrl templates ls [--category c] [--license class] [--search text] [flags]
```

Options:

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--category` | string |  | homelab, media, storage, games, devtools, ai, data, web, analytics, automation, productivity or security |
| `--license` | string |  | licence class: permissive, copyleft, source-available or proprietary |
| `--search` | string |  | search words (name, summary, tags, licence, database engines) |

### nebulactrl templates plan

Preflight an install (changes nothing).

```
nebulactrl templates plan <template> --project <p> --env <e> [--server <s>] [--input KEY=VALUE]... [flags]
```

Options:

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--env` | string |  | environment ID, slug or name |
| `--input` | stringArray |  | install input KEY=VALUE (repeatable) |
| `--project` | string |  | project ID, slug or name |
| `--server` | string |  | server ID or name (enables capacity and port checks) |

### nebulactrl templates rm

Delete a template stack.

```
nebulactrl templates rm <instance-id> --confirm <template-id> [--delete-volumes] [flags]
```

Options:

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--confirm` | string |  | the template id, to confirm |
| `--delete-volumes` | bool |  | also remove the stack's Docker volumes (data is lost) |

### nebulactrl templates show

Show a template: services, inputs and licence.

```
nebulactrl templates show <template>
```

### nebulactrl templates update

Show what a newer template revision changes, or stage it (--apply).

```
nebulactrl templates update <instance-id> [--apply] [--input KEY=VALUE]... [flags]
```

Without --apply this prints the diff between the template as installed and the catalog's current revision and changes nothing.
With --apply the changes marked 'apply' are staged as ordinary edits (nothing is deployed). Fields you changed are kept; databases, routes and services are never touched.

Options:

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--apply` | bool |  | stage the changes (default: only show them) |
| `--input` | stringArray |  | value for an input the new revision added, KEY=VALUE (repeatable) |

## nebulactrl vars

Manage service environment variables.

```
nebulactrl vars
```

### nebulactrl vars history

Show a variable's versions (secrets show a fingerprint only).

```
nebulactrl vars history <service> KEY
```

### nebulactrl vars ls

List variables (secret values are never shown).

```
nebulactrl vars ls <service> [flags]
```

Options:

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--exports` | bool |  | also list the virtual variables other services can reference |
| `--platform` | bool |  | also list the platform-provided variables |

### nebulactrl vars rm

Delete variables (staged until the next deploy).

```
nebulactrl vars rm <service> KEY...
```

### nebulactrl vars rotate

Replace a generated variable's value (staged, never deployed).

```
nebulactrl vars rotate <service> KEY [--dry-run] [flags]
```

Re-runs the generators of a variable created with ${{secret(..)}} and similar. --dry-run prints the plan only:
which services consume the value, in which order to deploy them, and any blockers. Without it the new
value is staged on this service and on every consumer; nothing is deployed. Database credentials
cannot be rotated this way once deployed.

Options:

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--dry-run` | bool |  | show the plan without staging anything |

### nebulactrl vars set

Set variables (staged until the next deploy).

```
nebulactrl vars set <service> KEY=VALUE... [--secret] [--scope build] [flags]
```

Upserts variables on a service. Changes are staged: run `services deploy` to apply them.
Values are never echoed. Use KEY=- to read a value from stdin, which keeps secrets out of the
shell history and process list. A variable that is already secret stays secret.

A value may contain generators that run once, on the server: KEY='${{secret(32)}}' stores a random
secret. Running the same command again keeps the generated value (use `vars rotate` to replace it).
Other forms: ${{service-slug.KEY}}, ${{KEY}}, ${{shared.KEY}}; write $${{ for a literal ${{.
--scope build passes the variable to image builds of git services (--build-arg, or a BuildKit secret
when it is secret); --scope both also keeps it in the container.

Options:

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--comment` | string |  | a note stored with the variable |
| `--scope` | string |  | where the variable is injected: runtime (default), build or both |
| `--secret` | bool |  | mark the variables as secret (write-only) |

### nebulactrl vars shared

Manage shared variables of the team (@team), a project (<project>) or an environment (<project>/<env>).

```
nebulactrl vars shared
```

#### nebulactrl vars shared ls

List shared variables.

```
nebulactrl vars shared ls <@team|project[/env]>
```

#### nebulactrl vars shared rm

Delete shared variables.

```
nebulactrl vars shared rm <@team|project[/env]> KEY...
```

#### nebulactrl vars shared rotate

Replace a generated shared variable (staged, never deployed).

```
nebulactrl vars shared rotate <@team|project[/env]> KEY [--dry-run] [flags]
```

Options:

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--dry-run` | bool |  | show the plan without staging anything |

#### nebulactrl vars shared set

Set shared variables (restages the services that use them).

```
nebulactrl vars shared set <@team|project[/env]> KEY=VALUE... [--secret] [flags]
```

Options:

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--secret` | bool |  | mark the variables as secret (write-only) |

#### nebulactrl vars shared share

Stage KEY=${{shared.KEY}} on services.

```
nebulactrl vars shared share <@team|project[/env]> KEY <service>...
```

A shared variable reaches a service only through an explicit reference row. This stages
KEY=${{shared.KEY}} on each service (services given as ID or project/env/slug).
